aiSummary.oneLiner: Advanced open-source autopilot software ecosystem for autonomous vehicles.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: ArduPilot is a highly advanced, open-source autopilot suite capable of controlling a vast array of autonomous vehicles. It supports multicopters, traditional helicopters, fixed-wing aircraft, rovers, submarines, and even antenna trackers. The firmware relies on a robust extended Kalman filter for precise state estimation using various sensors like GPS, IMUs, and barometers. Its highly modular architecture allows researchers and commercial operators to build highly customized, reliable autonomous systems for complex missions.
keyFeatures: Multi-vehicle support: Controls copters, planes, rovers, and submarines from a single unified codebase.
Advanced navigation: Utilizes complex extended Kalman filters for highly accurate positioning and attitude estimation.
Scripting engine: Supports onboard Lua scripting for implementing custom behaviors without recompiling firmware.
Hardware abstraction: Runs on dozens of different flight controller boards and architectures.
Extensive sensor support: Integrates seamlessly with hundreds of different GPS modules, rangefinders, and cameras.

useCases.title: Commercial drone delivery
useCases.description: Power autonomous delivery drones requiring highly reliable, beyond-visual-line-of-sight navigation.

useCases.title: Agricultural surveying
useCases.description: Control fixed-wing aircraft conducting large-scale crop mapping and analysis missions.

useCases.title: Academic research
useCases.description: Implement and test novel control algorithms or computer vision integration on physical hardware.

useCases.title: Custom robotics
useCases.description: Build unique autonomous rovers or boats using the flexible, hardware-agnostic firmware.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Aerospace engineers, robotics researchers, and commercial UAV manufacturers. It requires strong knowledge of C++, embedded systems, and control theory.
